Shrink Existing Checkpoint Files by Dropping Note Backtraces

Source: R/checkpoint_slim.R
compact_checkpoints.Rd

Checkpoints written by TempleCBE 0.11.1 and earlier keep the rlang backtraces that tune (2.0.0 and later) stores with each note in a tuning result's `.notes` column. A backtrace can reach the environments of the frames that raised a warning, so each saved note can carry its own copy of the training data, and a workflow's checkpoint can be many times the size of its metrics and predictions. Since 0.11.2 new checkpoints are written without them (see `options(templecbe.keep_note_traces)`); `compact_checkpoints()` rewrites checkpoints that are already on disk the same way, so a long run does not have to be recomputed to get the smaller files.

Usage

compact_checkpoints(dir, recursive = TRUE, dry_run = FALSE)

Arguments

dir

An existing checkpoint directory, such as the `checkpoint_dir` of [workflow_map_checkpointed()], [tune_grid_checkpointed()] or [fit_resamples_checkpointed()].

recursive

Logical (default `TRUE`). Also rewrite the files in the subdirectories of `dir` ([workflow_map_checkpointed()] keeps one subdirectory per workflow).

dry_run

Logical (default `FALSE`). When `TRUE`, only report the sizes the files would have, without changing them.

Value

A tibble, one row per `.rds` file, with columns `path`, `size_before` and `size_after` (bytes) and `action` (`"compacted"`, `"would compact"`, `"unchanged"` or `"unreadable"`), invisibly. A message reports the total saving.

Details

Each `.rds` file in `dir` is read, the backtraces of the tuning results it holds are set to `NULL` (keeping the note text, its type and location, and every fingerprint and attribute), and the file is replaced only when the new one is smaller. The new file is written next to the old one and renamed over it, so an interrupted run leaves either the old file or the new one. A file that holds no backtrace, or cannot be read, is left alone. A file is read with [readRDS()], which can run code stored in it: only point `dir` at checkpoints that you (or a process you trust) wrote.

See also

[clean_checkpoints()], [collect_checkpoints()]

Examples

# \donttest{
tmp <- file.path(tempdir(), "compact_demo")
dir.create(tmp)
saveRDS(list(a = 1), file.path(tmp, "ckpt_a.rds"))
compact_checkpoints(tmp, dry_run = TRUE)
#> compact_checkpoints(): would compact 0 of 1 file(s) in '/tmp/Rtmpn0GH9K/compact_demo', which would save 0.0 B.
unlink(tmp, recursive = TRUE)
# }
